messages.subject: Re: R key words not highlighted
messages.body_plain:
EXPLANATION:

When the vimcom.plus library is loaded by R, it reads the list of files at ~/.vim/r-plugin/objlist.
Every time that a command is entered on R prompt, the vimcom.plus library checks the number of loaded libraries. If there a change in this number, the vimcom.plus library writes the list of loaded libraries at /tmp/r-plugin-yourlogin/libnames_uniquename. If the newly loaded library isn't at ~/.vim/r-plugin-objlist directory yet, its fun_ and omnls_ files are created. Then, the vimcom.plus library sends to Vim a message to update the syntax highlight of functions and omnicompletion of objects. Vim reads the file /tmp/r-plugin-yourlogin/libnames_uniquename and checks whether the newly library files were already read from ~/.vim/r-plugin-objlist and, if not, it reads them (that is how you get the syntax highlight of function names updated).

The problem is: I can't use a TCP port to receive messages on Vim because the messages would mess with Vim's queue loop of events. I have to rely on the clientserver feature which depends on Vim being connect with a X Server. GVim is a graphical application and under Linux it is can only runs if connected to the X Server. Vim is a text mode application and doesn't need X Server to run. However, the text mode Vim running in a terminal emulator can connect to X Server, but you have to start Vim with the argument "--servername ANYNAME".

PRACTICAL ANSWER:

If you were running GVim, the syntax highlight of functions is automatically updated. If you were running Vim, you have to start it as in the example below:

vim --servername VIM filename.R

There is a tip in the documentation on how to create a bash function to call vim with the argument "--servername VIM", so we have to type less when running Vim. Please, look for "tvim" and "RpluginConfig" in the documentation.

messages.subject: Rmd files not detected/working?
messages.body_plain:
I'm happily using the latest version of vim-r-plugin on CentOS with a manually-compiled vim, and for .R files everything works very well. When I try to edit a .Rmd file however, the plugin does not seem to recognize it, which I can tell by not creating the R menu in gvim or allowing the /rf "start R" command to work. I can build the .Rmd file in question in Rstudio just fine.

Is there something special that must be done to enable it?

messages.subject: Re: Rmd files not detected/working?
messages.body_plain:
What directory is your Vim-R-plugin installed in? It seems that Vim only reads files from ftdetect directory if the directory is in ~/.vim. So, if your Vim-R-plugin directory is something else, you have to create a symbolic link to /path/to/Vim-R-plugin/ftdetect/r.vim at ~/.vim/ftdetect/r.vim (see
http://www.lepem.ufc.br/jaa/r-plugin.html#r-plugin-installation). Example:

mkdir ~/.vim/ftdetect
ln -s /path/to/Vim-R-plugin/ftdetect/r.vim ~/.vim/ftdetect/r.vim

Did you install the plugin at ~/.vim directory?

messages.body_plain:
On Sunday, February 16, 2014 6:23:27 PM UTC-3, Jakson Alves de Aquino wrote:
> It seems that Vim only reads files from ftdetect directory if the directory is in ~/.vim.

I've just discovered that the above statement is wrong. Vim reads files from ftdetect directories that are in its runtimepath. So the "filetype on" command in the vimrc must be written after configuring the runtimepath.
